final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity and low homolog frequency; disruptive substitution likely abolishes CBS activity.
Near-top pathogenicity with conserved position; strong LOF support.
Very high pathogenicity; low MSA coverage weakens evolutionary evidence but phenotype signal is primary.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are stable and high confidence; further tool calls are unlikely to change final selections.

history.rationale: K119 forms the covalent Schiff base with PLP; alanine substitution removes the catalytic lysine and should abolish activity.
Known PLP-binding lysine; mutation is expected to abolish catalytic activity.
Highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity (0.987) and low evolutionary frequency (0.056) support LOF; low ESM-1v plausibility is consistent with a disruptive mutation.
C52 is a heme axial ligand; replacing it with alanine disrupts heme coordination and likely impairs folding/stability.
Heme-coordinating cysteine; loss of heme binding likely impairs CBS function.
AlphaMissense 0.951 indicates strong loss-of-function; mutant frequency 0.218 is moderate and slightly weakens but does not overturn the high pathogenicity prediction.
H65 is the second heme axial ligand; alanine substitution should abolish heme binding and disrupt the active enzyme.
Heme-coordinating histidine; mutation likely disrupts cofactor binding.
Pathogenicity 0.845 is lower than others, but very low MSA frequency (0.046) and known heme-coordinating role keep it as a plausible but not top candidate.
T257 is a conserved PLP-binding residue; alanine likely weakens cofactor binding and catalytic activity.
Located near active site; plausible loss-of-function through altered substrate or PLP interactions.
Pathogenicity 0.913 is good but mutant frequency 0.238 suggests some evolutionary tolerance, reducing confidence relative to top candidates.
R266 participates in substrate/product carboxylate binding; alanine removes a key ionic interaction required for catalysis.
Conserved basic residue; may participate in substrate binding.
Pathogenicity 0.929 is strong and MSA frequency 0.083 supports a conserved, damaging position.
K384 is located in the catalytic core and likely contributes to substrate or PLP stabilization; alanine should impair activity.
Potential regulatory or ionic interaction site; mutation could impair activity.
High pathogenicity (0.949) but extremely low MSA coverage (0.103) reduces confidence in evolutionary context; still a plausible LOF candidate.
D376 may participate in proton transfer or active-site electrostatics; alanine substitution is expected to reduce catalysis.
Acidic residue possibly involved in catalysis or structural stability.
Very high pathogenicity score (0.979) drives strong LOF prediction; MSA coverage is only 0.103 so evolution evidence is unreliable, but phenotype remains the primary signal.
E176 is near the PLP-binding site and may help position catalytic residues; alanine should impair activity.
Surface acidic residue; may affect stability or interaction, but lower confidence.
Pathogenicity 0.910 supports LOF; MSA frequency 0.058 is low, consistent with a conserved position.
G256 is in the conserved PLP-binding loop; substitution to alanine may reduce loop flexibility and cofactor binding.
Glycine near active site; small size likely important for backbone flexibility.
Pathogenicity 0.807 is the lowest among the pool and MSA frequency 0.298 indicates notable tolerance, so confidence drops.
Y163 is near the active site and may contribute to substrate orientation; alanine likely disrupts efficient catalysis.
Aromatic residue possibly in hydrophobic core or substrate pocket; lower prior confidence.
AlphaMissense 0.985 is nearly as high as K119A, full MSA coverage with low mutant frequency (0.115) supports damaging effect; raised from rank 10.
